positive.prompt: Review this dashboard UX plan before implementation and identify missing interaction states.
Rate the design completeness of this responsive page plan and surface accessibility gaps.
Check whether this proposed workflow reuses our design system and resolves the user journey.

negative.prompt: Audit the live settings page in Chrome at mobile and desktop widths.
Implement the responsive account dashboard from this approved design.
Review the service migration plan for architecture, rollout safety, and failure modes.

evals.prompt: Review this dashboard plan without editing it: A signed-in user sees KPI cards and a recent-orders table. The page fetches both datasets and lets the user filter by month. The plan describes the successful populated view but no other UI states.
evals.expected_output: A read-only seven-pass design review that identifies the absent state behavior, gives evidence-based ratings, and proposes an implementation-facing state matrix without pretending the plan was updated.
expectations: Evaluates all seven passes and does not limit the review to loading behavior
Identifies applicable loading, empty, error, success, partial, disabled, permission, or offline states without manufacturing impossible states
Describes what users see, what actions remain available, and how recovery works
Distinguishes first-use empty data from a zero-result filtered state
Provides evidence for the initial score and defines what excellent completeness means for this dashboard
Keeps the review read-only and does not claim to have changed the source plan
Ends with a design-readiness verdict, unresolved decisions, not-in-scope items, and acceptance criteria

evals.prompt: Review this responsive page plan: Desktop has a persistent left sidebar, a six-column comparison table, breadcrumbs, and Save/Cancel actions. The only mobile requirement is 'stack on mobile.' Do not generate visuals.
evals.expected_output: A text-only design-plan review that turns the vague mobile statement into explicit unresolved viewport, navigation, data, action, zoom, and accessibility decisions.
expectations: Identifies 'stack on mobile' as insufficient because the sidebar, table, breadcrumbs, and actions each require intentional behavior
Uses a breakpoint behavior table or comparably compact artifact
Covers content priority, mobile navigation, dense-table alternatives, action reachability, overflow, zoom, keyboard, focus, and screen-reader considerations
Presents a recommended decision with rationale, alternatives, and impact rather than silently choosing a pattern
Respects the text-only instruction and neither generates nor offers unsolicited mockups
Avoids claiming WCAG conformance without runtime evidence

evals.prompt: Review a plan that proposes custom buttons, modal dialogs, toast notifications, spacing values, and status colors. The repository already documents equivalent Button, Dialog, Toast, spacing-token, and semantic-color primitives in DESIGN.md. Findings only.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-led review that prioritizes existing-system reuse and treats new components or values as intentional exceptions requiring rationale.
expectations: Inspects or references DESIGN.md and maps planned elements to the existing vocabulary
Recommends reuse based on semantic and state behavior, not visual similarity alone
Flags custom primitives and raw values as unjustified divergence unless a requirement cannot be met
Does not invent or redesign the design system
Labels recommendations as unapproved and makes no plan edits
Includes design-system alignment alongside the other six passes

evals.prompt: Review this landing-page plan: a purple gradient hero says 'Unlock the power of AI,' followed by three identical rounded feature cards, invented usage metrics, a testimonial carousel, and a final CTA. The plan gives no product-specific rationale.
evals.expected_output: A context-sensitive seven-pass critique that identifies unsupported claims and generic generated-design patterns, then recommends product-specific alternatives rather than swapping in another trend.
expectations: Classifies the surface as marketing before applying relevant design criteria
Flags generic copy, arbitrary gradient use, symmetric cards, excessive rounding, fake metrics, and purposeless carousel behavior with concrete rationale
Treats unsupported metrics as a trust problem, not merely a style preference
Tests brand clarity, section purpose, hierarchy, and whether each pattern earns its place
Proposes specific directions grounded in product goal and audience while leaving unresolved brand decisions open
Does not prescribe one universal aesthetic or reject a pattern solely because it exists

evals.prompt: Review the design of this plan: migrate an internal event-processing service to a new queue, add retries and dead-letter handling, backfill events, and roll out by traffic percentage. There are no dashboards, CLIs, operator controls, or user-facing changes.
evals.expected_output: A concise not-applicable verdict that routes the backend-only plan to engineering plan review instead of forcing design findings.
expectations: Recognizes that the plan has no user-facing or developer-facing interaction surface
Returns a Not applicable verdict
Routes the request to plan-eng-review for architecture, failure-mode, rollout, and test analysis
Does not invent screens, UI states, accessibility issues, or visual-design findings
Does not execute the seven design passes after the scope gate fails

evals.prompt: Read the attached checkout UX plan and give me findings only. Do not edit files, create TODOs, generate mockups, open a browser, or implement anything.
evals.expected_output: A complete read-only design review that honors every mutation and tooling boundary while still surfacing decisions and acceptance criteria.
expectations: States that the review is findings-only and performs no file mutation
Runs all seven passes when the checkout plan has design scope
Separates observed evidence, assumptions, recommendations, and unresolved decisions
Does not create TODO files, review logs, state files, mockups, browser sessions, or implementation code
Does not imply recommendations were accepted or incorporated
Includes approved visual references as none and reports evidence limitations
